headline: Stablecoins shed $14.5B in 30 days, long funding drops from 10% to 3% in a day, and BTC idles just above its 200-day average.
summary: Dollars are still leaving crypto, just through a different door: net of the USDT discount, the Coinbase premium is almost gone, yet stablecoin supply fell another 1.5% this week. Leveraged longs cooled off on their own while price went sideways, with open interest down about 7,000 BTC but still at the 97th percentile. The close sits 1.1% above the 200-day average; Friday brings PPI and the Deribit weekly expiry.

overview.lead: Sellers and leverage are both backing off: dollars keep leaving through stablecoin redemptions, longs trimmed while price drifted, and BTC sits above its 200-day average.
points: The narrower Coinbase discount mostly came from USDT trading below $1; stablecoins are what is actually shrinking (first finding).
Funding on the three-venue basis fell from 10.0% to 3.1% with no jump in liquidations (second finding).
Short-term holders are in a second day of concentrated loss-taking; realized loss is 4,796 BTC, just short of the 5,000 confirmation line (CheckOnChain).
Friday Nov 13: Deribit weekly expiry at 08:00 UTC, US October PPI at 13:30 UTC.

cycle.lead: Bull day 34, but the weekly regime score slipped to −0.06, its first negative reading since the Sep 22 flip; the 200-day average that defines the bull stage is still rising.
points: 63 straight closes above a rising 200-day average; the average was 72,044 thirty days ago and 73,118 today.

Only one of six evidence lights is on, realized cap (+0.18% over 30 days); 12-month momentum, MVRV vs its 1-year mean, exchange supply, the short-term holder cost and cost vs true market mean are all off.

The weekly score is on the bear side now, but a flip needs 4 weeks below zero and this is week 1; the Dawn Index heat is 36.5, still in Daybreak. Heat measures valuation and the weekly score leans on trend: one reads cool, the other is weakening.
At the last 30 days' pace, a straight-line extrapolation puts the short-term holder cost crossing above the true market mean near Dec 21, 3 days later than yesterday's estimate.

market.lead: Quiet, low-volume sideways trade: volume fell by a third, the close landed mid-range, and the up-leg is 0.4% from its 15% reversal line.
points: The leg from the Jun 30 low of 58,532 is 134 days old and 14.6% off its 86,594 high; a close below 73,605 starts a new down-leg.

Sell Pressure Index 100 with momentum 0.17: day 2 of the bottom combination. After the past 20, price was up 30 days later 11 times with a +1.8% median, about the same as any day's +3.2%; only 5 of the 8 cases from 2018–2022 were profitable at exit.

deriv.lead: Some leverage left, but the crowding has not cleared: funding cooled, yet 74.7% of Binance accounts are still long, the 95th percentile of the past year.
points: This page's finding: five-venue funding went from 7.1% to 5.4%; open interest is 338,130 BTC, still the 97th percentile since 2021.

Estimated long liquidation band at 71.0–72.7K, 2.9% below the close, about 27K BTC (estimate, seven venues via Coinalyze); a move into it would trigger forced market selling that could speed up a drop.
25-delta risk reversal −3.8 → −3.5, so the put premium eased a little; implied vol is 34.7% at 7 days and 38.2% at 90 days, near-dated is cheaper and the curve is not inverted.
Friday's expiry holds 33,086 BTC (9.4%) with max pain at 76,000; calls cluster at 81,000 and puts at 72,000.

flows.lead: The dollar exit has not stopped: ETFs lost $1.87B over 20 trading days and entered an outflow stretch on Nov 9, while stablecoins fell another 1.5% this week.
points: This page's finding: net of USDT, the Coinbase premium 7-day average is −0.008%, right at its 4-year 10th percentile; USDT itself is at 0.9988, with its 7-day discount at the 2.7th percentile of the past four years.
ETFs: −$1.62B over 7 trading days (to Nov 10, CoinMarketCap); Nov 10 alone was −$115M, Farside shows −$95M.
The 20-day sum crossed the −$1.5B stretch line only 2 days ago; the past 5 stretches bottomed as deep as −$5.6B (June 2026), and the 30 days after they ended went both ways.
Realized cap +0.18% over 30 days, a small inflow; the 2-year yield is 0.73 points above the Fed's upper bound (Nov 10), so bonds price a hike.

onchain.lead: Short-term holders keep selling at a loss without turning it into capitulation: day 2 of concentrated loss-taking, with realized losses edging up only slightly.
points: Short-term holder loss intensity is 2.99 (above 2 counts as concentrated); they realized $433M of losses in a day against $116M of profit (Bitview).
STH-SOPR 0.9886, below 1 for 6 straight days; CheckOnChain's realized loss is 4,796 BTC, about 300 more than the day before.
Network net realized P/L was −$549M on Nov 10 and −$1.78B over 7 days, slightly less than the prior 7 days (CoinMetrics).
By address balance tiers, 1K–10K BTC addresses have grown 11 days running and 100–1K BTC addresses have shrunk 9 days running (Bitview); an address is not an entity.

news.title: MSCI's November review is final: Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi are deleted from its global indexes after the Nov 30 close
news.read: JPMorgan had estimated about $2.8B of passive selling if Strategy were removed; that selling is in MSTR shares, not BTC, and Strategy says MSCI-linked funds hold about 13M shares, under one day's volume. For BTC the effect is harder treasury-company fundraising at a time when treasury demand has already faded and ETFs lost $1.87B in 20 days: one buyer fewer. The cycle read is unchanged.

news.title: Spot BTC ETFs lost $95M on Nov 10, a fourth straight outflow day; BlackRock's IBIT shed $78.2M, its eighth straight session
news.read: Outflows are shrinking (about $400M each on Nov 5 and 6) but have not stopped; on this site's CoinMarketCap basis the day was −$115M and 7 trading days total −$1.62B. The estimated ETF holder cost sits about 6% above the close, so this group is under water as a whole, and whether outflows stop depends on price getting back near that cost.

news.title: CME FedWatch puts the odds of a hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting at 90%; October CPI rose 0.4% m/m, core 0.3%
news.read: Markets treat the hike as settled; the 2-year yield at 0.73 points over the Fed's upper bound says the same. For BTC it means costlier money, the same direction as stablecoin redemptions and ETF outflows; it does not touch the market-stage call, which only uses the 200-day average.

news.title: CoreWeave beat estimates and jumped 14% premarket, lifting Nasdaq-100 futures about 2%; BTC did not follow and stayed under 74,000
news.read: BTC falls with stocks but does not rise with them; its win rate against the S&P 500 over the last 90 US sessions is exactly 50%. The link to AI stocks is tighter on down days and held that way here; Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings will test the asymmetry again.

news.title: The dollar index neared 103, up about 1% in 24 hours and the highest since April 2025; gold sat just above $4,000/oz
news.read: A firmer dollar and hike expectations are the same force, a headwind for risk assets; BTC's 30-day correlation with the dollar index on this site is only −0.13, so this is background rather than the daily driver.

news.title: CoinGlass: $725M of crypto liquidations in 24 hours, $200M of it BTC and 85% longs; Binance funding 0.0078%, below the 0.01% baseline
news.read: That was the CPI-day wave; afterwards funding and open interest both fell, and this site's Coinalyze count of Nov 11 long liquidations is only $17.9M, so the later drop was voluntary closing. The two liquidation datasets are built differently, so totals are not compared.

news.title: The London Stock Exchange eased listing guidance for professional-only crypto ETNs, opening the way for leveraged BTC and ETH products
news.read: Another leveraged channel for institutions adds demand capacity over time; it is open only to professional investors, so near-term money is small and it does not change the current ETF outflow picture.

news.title: Deutsche Bank's digital asset custody for European institutional clients is live, covering BTC, ETH and stablecoins, with Asia next
news.read: Big-bank custody is plumbing for institutional entry and works on a scale of years; today's flows are stablecoin redemptions and ETF outflows, so this does not change the short-term read.

findings.title: Coinbase discount narrows as dollars leave via stablecoin redemptions
findings.lean_why: Stablecoins that could buy BTC fell $14.5B in a month, so buyers have less dry powder; the US spot discount itself is small.
findings.what: The US discount is actually small; most of it was USDT trading below $1. Net of that, the Coinbase premium 7-day average is just −0.008%, versus −0.14% unadjusted (Nov 11).
findings.why: Split apart, it is two things. USDT is at 0.9988 with a 7-day discount of −0.13%, the 2.7th percentile of the past four years; over the same stretch stablecoin supply fell to $289.5B, down $14.5B in 30 days and 1.5% in a week (DefiLlama). That is people redeeming stablecoins for dollars, and Glassnode's Nov 11 weekly also shows a $14.2B 30-day contraction, the fastest since June 2022. US spot has not improved: Coinbase spot takers sold 4,887 BTC more than they bought over 7 days, the 4th percentile of the past four years (Coinalyze), and ETFs lost $1.87B over 20 trading days (CoinMarketCap).
findings.alt: The USDT discount may also reflect weak USDT-quoted demand on Binance rather than redemptions alone; stablecoin supply here is DefiLlama's all-USD stablecoins and differs from Glassnode's figure by a few hundred million. The 7-day premium lags by several days, and the single-day reading of −0.0003% is already near zero.
findings.history: Stablecoin supply has dropped this fast in a week 13 times since 2020, and the 30-day median price change afterwards was +4.2%, about the same as any day's +2.3%. The Coinbase premium 7-day average has jumped like this 10 times since 2022 with a +9.7% 30-day median, yet 3 of the last 5 were followed by declines.
findings.so: What changes is the reading: US demand is not as weak as it looked, and the thing to track is now stablecoins. The direction does not change: ETFs, Coinbase spot and stablecoins are all still draining, and the Nov 6 finding that all three dollar pipes were shrinking is confirmed today.
findings.next: By Nov 18, two paths: stablecoin supply below $287B means redemptions are still accelerating, a confirmation; a positive weekly change means the exit has paused, a refutation.

findings.title: Longs left without being liquidated: funding fell from 10% to 3% in a day
findings.lean_why: Crowded longs shrank while price held, leaving less fuel for a liquidation cascade below; open interest is still at the 97th percentile and only eased a little.
findings.what: Longs are cooling off, and leaving on their own: funding on the three-venue basis dropped from 10.0% to 3.1%, and open interest fell about 7,000 BTC (Nov 11).
findings.why: No signal flagged this; it comes from per-venue funding and open interest. By venue, Hyperliquid fell most, from a 10.5% 7-day average to 0.2%; Binance 7.9% → 7.3% and Bybit 7.7% → 5.8% moved the same way. Liquidations did not pick up: longs saw only $17.9M of forced closes against $21.4M for shorts (Coinalyze), and price closed up 0.3%. Open interest went from 345,129 to 338,130 BTC, mostly voluntary closing. The contradiction is that 74.7% of Binance accounts are still long, the 95th percentile of the past year.
findings.alt: Hyperliquid settles hourly and this is a snapshot, so its rate can swing a lot within an hour or two; the five-venue weighted rate only fell from 7.1% to 5.4%. A 2% one-day drop in open interest could also be market makers or basis trades reducing, not only longs; this is a single day of data.
findings.history: The 7-day funding average (Coinalyze) is 7.6%, the 62nd percentile since 2021 and far from negative; it has turned negative 13 times, with price higher 90 days later in 10. Leverage built against price this month: open interest is up 9.6% in 30 days while price fell 9.6%.
findings.so: What changes is liquidation risk: with fewer longs, a move into the estimated 71.0–72.7K band would cascade less. What does not change is the crowding, with the long-account share and open interest both above the 95th percentile; the Nov 7 finding about longs piling in at nearly 10% funding is moving toward refutation.
findings.next: By Nov 18, two paths: open interest below 330,000 BTC means leverage is really unwinding, a confirmation; three-venue funding back above 8% means today was snapshot noise, a refutation.

research.summary: Glassnode's new Nov 11 The Week On-chain agrees with this site's readings: price below the 75.6K short-term holder cost, 62–66K as the only dense supply below, and stablecoins shrinking fastest; nothing new from K33, The Block Research or Coinbase Institutional.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Running on Empty
items.points: BTC near 74K, below the 75.6K short-term holder cost, with only about 35% of short-term coins in profit; true market mean 77.5K; two-thirds of short-term supply sits above price up to 83.6K, and the only dense block below is 62–66K. Stablecoins shrank $14.2B in 30 days, the fastest since June 2022; ETFs lost $1.6B over 20 sessions. The largest long liquidation cluster is 59.5–62.6K; since Nov 5, bids within 5% of price have outweighed asks every hour, with the largest at 68–72.5K. Wallets of 100–1K and 1K–10K BTC score above 0.5 on accumulation. Holding the June low of 58.5K keeps the August trend change intact; a sustained break below 73K points to a longer consolidation.
items.meaning: The dense 62–66K block is the Nov 10 second finding, and the stablecoin redemption is today's first finding. Its ETF 20-day −$1.6B uses a different basis from this site's CoinMarketCap −$1.87B; by address balance tiers this site sees 100–1K BTC addresses down 25K BTC in a week, the opposite of its entity-based accumulation score, so the two are not compared in size.

items.title: NOWPayments + Glassnode: Stablecoins in Commerce
items.points: 86% of NOWPayments' stablecoin receipts run on USDT over Tron, BNB Chain and Ethereum; stablecoin supply exceeds $300B.
items.meaning: A payments report with no BTC market analysis; its stablecoin total uses a different basis from this site's DefiLlama $289.5B.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 46
items.points: BTC near 75K, the lowest since August; futures open interest of $37B fell only 1.1%, long funding payments stayed above the high band; 25-delta skew 11.1%; ETFs lost $1.6B in the week; conclusion: defensive, crowded longs, but some leverage already cleared.
items.meaning: Some leverage clearing only looks true as of Nov 11: three-venue funding fell from 10.0% to 3.1% and open interest dropped about 7,000 BTC; a 74.7% long-account share is still crowded.
